Every other cell is reproduced on all 11,930 records.

submitted_defect.defect: the file lacks the PRCDCSAD rows its released program writes
submitted_defect.reason: The submitted interim file is inconsistent with its released program: yamaa writes 1,156 PRCDCSAD rows (presence of CDC-defined symptoms) that the file does not have, and every other cell matches. adc19ef-ia.sas gives FATIGUE, HEADACHE, RIHNRA and NAUSEA grp = 2 (symp_all_1; the interim ADSYMPT has 1,494 such records); symp_all_4 keeps the last record of each analysis visit and group (keepflg, grp < 20) and symp2 to symp5 keep every one; adc19ef_1 names it PARAMCD = 'PRCDCSAD' and writes it with an unconditional output, then writes the CDCONST record of the same record; adc19ef_3 keeps every record with a PARAMCD; the final step drops only PARAMCD in ("CDCONST", "ST1PD", "ST17PD", "ST2PD", "ST214PD", "ST214CD", "ST214SE", "ST1PDA", "ST17PDA", "ST2PDA", "ST214PDA") and the CDC flag columns, and the closing proc sort has no nodupkey. No macro, %include or where clause touches these rows. The CDCONST records did exist when the file was made: ST1CD ends at the first CDC onset, before ST1SE, for 109 subjects without a severe onset. The file was therefore not produced by the program text as released; nothing in the program or the data supports dropping the rows, so the spec keeps them.

missing_input.missing: DM.BRTHDTC and two subjects' height and BMI (redacted); the Japanese-participants list the program imports; one DS record the interim ADaM read, which the released interim DS does not carry
missing_input.reason: As in the final EUA ADSL: birth dates are redacted (ages at Dose 1, one imputation flag), VS redacts two subjects' height and BMI, and JPNFL comes from japanese-participants.xls, which is not in the release. One subject's EOTDCDT (2020-11-04) comes from a vaccination-phase disposition event other than COMPLETED; the released interim DS has only the subject's COMPLETED record.
